_comment: S5 of docs/STRICT-SCIENCE.md. Every coefficient or correction that moves a number the USER sees must be declared here as 'fit' (tuned against residuals, must name the artifact) or 'provisional' (hand-picked, not yet validated). Provisional is allowed, but it is surfaced here and must never be described to the user as truth. The integrity gate (integrity_gate.py) fails if a knob is missing status/note, or claims 'fit' without a fit_against artifact.

knobs.name: offshore_chl_distrust.magnitudes
knobs.note: Hand-chosen to pull over-optimistic offshore visibility toward a 15ft green floor after the Northeast Bank miss (app said 44ft, diver saw 15-20ft green). Directionally defensible (satellite is surface-blind offshore) but the magnitudes are NOT fit to residuals. Must be refit once the loop accumulates offshore ground truth.

knobs.name: viz_predict.coefficients
knobs.note: The visibility model's turbidity/chl/wind/swell coefficients are expert-set, not regression-fit. Current hindcast on the handful of scored pairs shows r near 0, we do not yet have evidence they track reality. Refitting against residuals.jsonl is Phase 2 of the remediation plan.

knobs.name: sst_breaks.front_tracing
knobs.affects: which SST fronts draw as temperature-break lines on the map
knobs.note: Recalibrated 2026-08-12 after the San Nicolas/Tanner miss: the warm-pool west wall held 1.0-1.85 degC per 30 km (a textbook fishable break) but MUR smears fronts, capping its local gradient at 0.06-0.08 — below the old 0.1 seed, so the whole wall was invisible. New calibration on the 2026-08-09 grid: seed 0.06 / continue 0.035 / span 30 km traces the wall continuously on 3 consecutive days (55/57/37 fronts statewide, 1.5% of ocean px). Fronts peaking >= 0.1 style as strong (solid/bold), softer ones thin/dashed. To earn fit, validate traced lines against reported break crossings.

knobs.name: paddy_sink.SINK_SIGMA
knobs.affects: sunkFrac in the Track-a-paddy forecast — what share of drift runs are reported sunk, and so which runs the corridor width is computed from
knobs.note: Spread of the per-member lognormal sink threshold (median 1 = the median raft's float life). Derived from published values, NOT fitted to our data: warm-water median 22 d (Graiff/Rothausler) with the longest Bight rafts tracked at 63-109 d (Hobday 2000); treating 63 d as a ~99th-percentile survivor gives sigma = ln(63/22)/z(0.99) = 1.052/2.326 = 0.45. Cannot be fitted until a tracked paddy is re-sighted — no such observation exists in this app.

knobs.name: paddy_sink.LIFE_anchors
knobs.affects: float-life estimate in the origin block and the fouling rate driving sunkFrac
knobs.note: Literature medians for Macrocystis raft survival: ~41 d cool, ~22 d at/above 19 degC (sub-lethal stress, bryozoan fouling ballast is the kill mechanism rather than heat), ~14 d above 24 degC (hard-sink regime). Max observed 63-109 d. Pinned by tests so a change to a cited number fails CI and has to come with a citation.

knobs.name: reports.thresholds
knobs.where: pipeline/reports/thresholds.py (WIND_KT, GUST_OUTSIDE_KT, SEAS_FT, SANTA_ANA_*, FOG_LEVEL, SURF_FT, EXPOSURE_SCALE, LONG_PERIOD_S, ONSHORE_WIND_KT)
knobs.affects: Morning Report verdicts (within / marginal / outside our thresholds) for shore dives and boat ranges
knobs.note: Our own tiers, synthesized from DAN guidance (head-high surf, current), dive logs and practitioner consensus; the official triggers they sit beside (NWS headlines, the NWS San Diego steepness rule, rip current risk, the county 72-hour rain guidance) are sourced, not tuned. Shown to readers as 'our thresholds', never as standards. Offshore wind tiers were loosened from the research proposal (10/15 kt) to 15/20 kt after the first live run (2026-10-15) marked the ordinary 'NW 10 to 15 kt' day marginal at every offshore range; NWS's own advisory trigger is 21 kt. To earn fit: score archived verdicts against lifeguard closures, Coast Guard/harbor patrol incidents and diver reports of conditions. Evidence: Projects/ShouldIDive/fish-reports-research.md section 6.

knobs.name: reports.site_exposure
knobs.affects: which shore entries count as facing the swell, at an angle, or in its lee, and so the surf-at-entry estimate
knobs.note: Entry orientations are the CDIP MOP points' published shore normals (D0482, D0500, D0324, OC283). Exposure classes use 60/100 degree cutoffs, overridden by MOP itself when the modeled set height at the entry is under 40% (sheltered) or 75%+ (exposed) of the county surf forecast. The ratios and cutoffs are hand-set. Surf at the entry is MOP Hs x 1.27 (Rayleigh mean of the highest tenth), falling back to county sets scaled 1.0/0.6/0.35 by exposure when MOP is missing.

knobs.name: reports.hunting_vis
knobs.note: 10 ft is Reef Check California's minimum for fish counts; 15 ft for pelagics is an inference from how close yellowtail let a diver approach (8-12 ft, spearfishing lore). Not fit to any outcome data.

knobs.name: reports.fishing_profiles
knobs.where: pipeline/reports/fish.py (PELAGICS bite/tolerated bands and season weights; break min step 0.5F, search radius 18 km, MUR gradient seed 0.06 C/km; ambient cue rule 60%)
knobs.affects: the fishing view's species picture and named-spot table
knobs.note: Bands and seasons from the 2026-10-15 research pass (Runcie 2019, Block 1997, Squire 1982, Marin-Enriquez 2018, CPFV records); the same evidence base as Pelagic Lab's profiles. To earn fit: hindcast each day's profile status against the next days' fleet stops and, once licensed, dock counts.

knobs.name: reports.vis_bias_correction
knobs.where: pipeline/reports/visibility.py (calibrations: per-area geometric-mean ratio of posted / predicted p50 over the last 60 days of pairs, La Jolla and Laguna; an area under 15 pairs uses the ratio pooled over all areas; band = 15th-85th percentile of log residuals)
knobs.affects: the Ocean Report's predicted visibility numbers, map layer and highlights (not the main map), per area
knobs.note: Fit 2026-10-15. La Jolla: 50 Just Get Wet pairs (Aug 15-Oct 14), published p50 about twice the posts (ratio 0.48), r = 0.38; the ratio beat a flat offset (72% vs 62% inside the posted range, MAE 2.6 vs 2.8 ft). Laguna: 36 South Coast Divers pairs (Aug 4-Oct 15, read deterministically from the posts), the model sat at 27-29 ft while posts ran 0-20 ft: ratio 0.27, r = 0.70 but scaled MAE 3.3 ft, no better than always saying the average (3.2) and worse than repeating the previous post (2.8). La Jolla likewise: 2.6 vs 2.7 (average) and 2.4 (previous post). The correction fixes scale, not day-to-day skill; each build reports both baselines next to the model. Approved diver reports within 6 nm of an area's reference point join its pairs. Refit every build (seed + the report archive's own daily predictions at each area's reference point). Elsewhere the ratio is blended between the areas by inverse squared distance to their reference points (no seam), an extrapolation for islands and offshore. Pacific Wilderness (San Pedro, ingested from 2026-10-15, not in the fit): its posts since Aug give 13 site readings, Aug 7-Sep 24 (7 with a stated dive day, 9 inside the 60-day window), short of 15, so there is no Palos Verdes area. Paired with the published p50 at each site (latest grid per UTC day): ratio 0.92, r = 0.65 (mostly oil rigs against shore), scaled MAE 10.5 ft (11.4 leave-one-out) against 14.6 for always saying the average and 17.9 for repeating the previous post; Palos Verdes shore alone (n = 9): ratio 0.81, r = 0.23, MAE 9.7 against 9.3 for the average. The blend applies 0.27-0.30 there (Laguna-weighted). If these few posts hold up, the report states LA-area and Catalina visibility at about a third of what divers find; weekly recaps may lean to good dives, so this is a lead, not a fit.
